plan: My private value is $20. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This prevents overpaying if I win and ensures I win when the item is worth more to me than others. Since values are randomly drawn, I can't predict others' values. By bidding $20, I maximize my potential profit - I'll win if others bid less, and pay only the second-highest bid. This strategy minimizes risk of significant loss.

My value is $29. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. Since the prize is randomly drawn each round and other bidders are rational, bidding exactly $29 maximizes my expected profit. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me.

With a private value of $45, my optimal strategy is to bid strategically. Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, I want to bid close to my true value but not exactly at it. I'll bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. A bid around $44-$45 range protects my potential earnings while giving me a good chance of winning. The key is to win without overpaying relative to my true value.
